title: Raspberry Pi 5 + Hailo-8: object detection FPS and mAP
dek: INT8 on the Hailo-8 NPU. YOLOv9-M runs 30.1 FPS at 53.3 mAP, YOLOX-S 95.8 FPS at 41.1 mAP. 10 models measured on a Pi 5.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: For 30 FPS on a Raspberry Pi 5 with a Hailo-8, use YOLOv9-M: 53.3 mAP at 30.1 FPS, MIT license. YOLOv9-C is the most accurate model here at 54.8 mAP but runs at 21.2 FPS. Above 60 FPS, YOLOX-S gives 41.1 mAP at 95.8 FPS. Every row runs INT8 on the NPU, so the mAP already includes the quantization loss.

blocks.caption: All 10 measured detectors on Raspberry Pi 5 + Hailo-8, INT8, batch 1, by throughput.

blocks.text: Two rows look broken. YOLOv9-T and YOLOv9-S score far below the same models in FP32 on the Pi CPU, and below YOLOX-Tiny. YOLOv9-M and YOLOv9-C barely lose anything. Treat T and S as a bad INT8 compile, not as what those models can do on a Hailo-8, until they are rerun.
YOLOX-Tiny is the fastest row at 195.6 FPS, but it runs at 416 px. Every other model here runs at 640 px.

blocks.title: Which model for your frame rate

blocks.caption: All 10 measured detectors on Raspberry Pi 5 + Hailo-8, INT8, batch 1, by mAP@50-95.

blocks.text: YOLO-NAS-L reaches 52.4 mAP at 15.4 FPS. YOLOv9-M beats it on both accuracy and speed, and YOLO-NAS weights come with a license that restricts commercial use. Without the Hailo-8, the same Pi tops out at 30 FPS with a much weaker model: see [the CPU-only Pi 5 guide](/articles/best-object-detection-rpi5).
